trace_steps: frame_retriever returns the unsolved geometry diagram at 27.0s as the strongest candidate (frame_27.00.png, relevance_score 0.6333), with nearby matching candidates at 26.5s and 28.0s, so these frames are the answer-critical visual phase.

On the same diagram, chart_analyzer's frame-level read for frame_26.50.png reports points A, B, C, D with A, B, D on one line, segments AC, BC, and CD drawn, ∠CAB marked 100°, AC = AD by matching double tick marks, and BC equal to AD; OCR across 26.5s/27.0s/28.0s confirms the printed givens 'AD = BC' and '100°' (avg detection confidence 0.9636).

From those givens, AD = BC and AC = AD imply AC = AD = BC, so triangle ACD is isosceles with AC = AD and triangle BCD is isosceles with BC = BD not actually grounded; the only directly grounded equalities are AC = AD and AD = BC, hence AC = AD = BC.

Using the grounded equalities, triangle ACD has vertex angle ∠CAD = 100° because chart_analyzer identifies the 100° angle at A between AC and the base line through A-B-D. Therefore the base angles of triangle ACD are (180° - 100°) / 2 = 40° each, so ∠CDA = 40°.
Since A, B, and D are collinear with B between A and D in the chart_analyzer frame-level read, ray DB is the same direction as ray DA at vertex D. Thus the asked green angle ∠BDC equals ∠CDA = 40°.
So the measure of angle BDC is 40°, which matches option D.
